Definition: from G4289; predisposition, i.e. alacrity:--forwardness of mind, readiness (of mind), ready (willing) mind.
BiblicalUsage: Prothymia means readiness of mind, willingness, forwardness. Paul says to the Corinthians that as there was a readiness to will, so there should be a performance, and if there be first a willing mind, it is accepted according to that a man hath. He boasts of the forwardness of their mind to the Macedonians. And the Bereans received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe readiness is the gift God accepts before the gift itself: a willing mind is accepted according to what a man has, not what he has not. I hold that the Bereans show me what readiness looks like, receiving the word eagerly and then searching it daily to see if it is true.
